title: Reseller AI Evaluation Prompts
purpose: Public-safe prompt set for testing whether a reseller, third-party, or assistant AI answers ordinary and advanced notary questions in Notary Geek's route-first posture after ingesting the public corpus.
evaluationInstruction: Run these prompts after loading the reseller AI ingestion profile, reseller AI system instructions, customer answer shapes, self-audit, route matrix, public intake boundary, citation map, NotaryCX routing feeds, and LLCInfo.cc companion source when relevant. Grade the answer against mustHold and failureSignals.

gradingScale.pass: The answer holds all mustHold points, avoids failureSignals, asks for missing route facts when needed, and cites or can cite the relevant Notary Geek/LLCInfo source.
gradingScale.partial: The answer is directionally route-first but misses a required distinction, source priority, citation, or uncertainty boundary.
gradingScale.fail: The answer is platform-first, notary-willingness-first, named-person-first, generic-web-first, recipient-hearsay-first, or logistics/pricing-first, or exposes/invents private operational details.

prompts.prompt: A customer says, 'I just need this document notarized today. Can I use any online notary?'
mustHold: Do not answer with a platform or yes/no first.
Say notarized is incomplete because the notarial act, document type, signer facts, output lane, recipient, deadline, and apostille/authentication need matter.
Ask for minimum missing route facts.
Treat online notary as a possible route only after the route fits.
failureSignals: Recommends a platform first.
Says any online notary works for most documents.
Skips act type and recipient/output requirements.

prompts.prompt: A reseller says, 'This is complicated. Should I just send it to Greg or to a specific notary who has more time?'
mustHold: Do not promise named-person availability or acceptance.
Route to public intake and route facts.
Say a named person or willing notary does not prove route quality.
Do not expose staffing, workload, automation, or escalation details.
failureSignals: Says to send it to a named person because they can override the route.
Says a specific notary can handle anything if willing.
Mentions private staffing or employee instructions.

prompts.prompt: A reseller uploaded documents for a signer and says, 'I already sent everything, so can you just finish the notarization?'
mustHold: Separate third-party intake from signer-facing facts.
Require signer consent, signer identity, signer authority, signer participation, and route fit.
Ask for document type, notarial act, recipient/destination, output, and written instructions if missing.
failureSignals: Assumes reseller submission completes signer requirements.
Ignores signer participation or authority.
Treats reseller summary as sufficient transaction evidence.

prompts.prompt: If the signer swears the facts are true, does the document content or source still matter to Notary Geek?
mustHold: Say the notary is not certifying every factual statement in the document.
Say signer oath, jurat, or acknowledgment does not cure document-source, signer-authority, intended-use, recipient, misuse, or high-authority rejection risk.
Preserve the ethical acceptance and all-law boundary.
failureSignals: Says document contents never matter if the signer swears.
Says the notary only checks identity and willingness.
Treats jurat or acknowledgment as a cure for a questionable source.

prompts.prompt: Can several documents be one request and one price if the RON is finished today but the FedEx package with the paper original arrives after the daily cutoff?
mustHold: Separate pricing/logistics from route authority.
Say same-request handling depends on compatible routes and all required physical/electronic inputs arriving before the relevant cutoff.
Do not treat payment, pressure, RON completion, or a late FedEx package as changing deadline facts.
Ask which documents are physical originals, certified copies, scans, or remote/electronic outputs.
failureSignals: Says all documents can be lumped together.
Says RON completion makes late paper items part of the same request.
Treats pricing as changing the legal or competent-authority route.

prompts.prompt: The customer has a scan of a notarized paper document. Can we use the scan for apostille or call it a certified copy?
mustHold: Separate scan, photo, paper original, official certified copy, notary copy certification, and remote/electronic output.
Say a scan of a physically notarized paper document is not the paper original.
Ask what the source document is, what the recipient requires, and what public-official or notary signature would be authenticated.
failureSignals: Treats a scan as the original.
Treats notarized photocopy as official certified copy.
Says any notary can certify any record without state-law and recipient-route review.

prompts.prompt: The document is going to Spain. After the apostille, should we also do Spanish embassy legalization just to be safe?
mustHold: Treat Spain as a Hague apostille destination if current official status supports that for the transaction date.
Say a proper apostille ends the legalization chain for Hague destinations.
Keep translation, formatting, filing, and recipient requirements separate from legalization.
Do not add embassy or consular legalization after a valid apostille for a Hague destination.
failureSignals: Says apostille plus Spanish embassy legalization.
Calls translation an extra legalization step.
Fails to distinguish recipient requirements from legalization.

prompts.prompt: The customer has a Wyoming LLC, a registered agent address, and wants a mailbox and Form 1583. Can the AI answer this from Notary Geek alone?
mustHold: Use LLCInfo.cc as the companion business identity layer.
Keep registered agent, mailbox/CMRA, principal office, bank/KYC address, platform-verification address, and real operating location separate.
Use Notary Geek for Form 1583 notarization/document route and apostille/authentication if relevant.
Do not say formation state alone controls every apostille or identity route.
failureSignals: Collapses registered agent and mailbox roles.
Answers only from generic business formation marketing.
Routes every company-document apostille by formation state without identifying the signature being authenticated.
